ops.description: The watchdisc lane's codex adversarial review surfaced parse-layer parity divergences affecting ALL consumers (watch delegates to parse_entry; triaged out-of-scope there). Fix in a dedicated lane; parse.rs is free once the smallmods lane lands. Items: (1) empty `usage:{}` drop semantics; (2) value type-filtering at parse (cwd:7, isSidechain:1 must preserve per trap #4); (3) tool-result non-str/list content handling; (4) empty toolDenialKind fallback; (5) huge-int/inf materialization behavior; (6) naive/leap-second timestamp parsing vs Python fromisoformat; (7) whitespace-driven interrupted/agent-injected flags (protocol.rs/filterspec boundary — check against Python str semantics per trap #1); (8) NESTED-object field reads during struct construction read first-wins pre-normalization; (9) ROOT dup keys — INCLUDING the `type` dispatch read — read first-wins: ACCEPTED PERMANENT DIVERGENCE, decided after cross-validated measurement (full root scan 274-425ns/record ≈ 7-20%; even a single last-wins type read costs 54-57ns ≈ 2.2-2.7% via sonic's ~5ns/key iteration; parse budget is ≤2%). Dup keys never occur in machine-generated transcripts; the Python reference dies at P6, making Rust behavior the contract (command-lane precedent). Divergence-pin tests + commit-body documentation land with the smallmods lane. Items 8-9 need NO further work unless a zero-cost mechanism appears. Remaining items 1-7: reproduce vs Python first, mirror exactly, pin in parse-level tests, respect the ≤2% parse budget. Read traps doc 62cd44cd first. MUST land before P3 gates.
